findings.title: The invocation frames the oath and warning
findings.claim: The divine name in the opening invocation takes on a framing force in this pericope: the utterance proceeds from that naming formula through an oath, a diagnosis of loss, and an exception that names a way through it.
findings.mechanism: Ismi carries the ordinary sense of a name or designation, and Allah is the Creator's unique name. The immediately following oath by time, then the diagnosis and exception, places the invoked designation at the head of a compact warning-and-response utterance. The naming branch's source-image of raising a name can color that position as an elevated designation.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening phrase becomes part of how the warning speaks: the name is invoked before the oath and judgment, so the short pericope opens under an addressed divine name.
findings.containment: The primary sense remains an invocation in Allah's name. This is a qualified reading of rhetorical sequence; it does not turn the basmala into an oath or establish legal authority.

epistemic.reason: The supplied context gives the oath and warning sequence, and trusted publication evidence agrees with legacy retrospective readings. The framing and raised-designation relation remain interpretive.

findings.title: Mercy frames loss and its exception
findings.claim: The two mercy epithets frame the diagnosis of human loss and the exception that follows as a course of beneficence already named at the opening.
findings.mechanism: The paired focus adjectives carry divine mercy as both inward compassion and active sparing and good-doing. They precede the human's placement in loss in 103:2 and the believing, good action, and mutual support of 103:3, so the pericope's diagnosis and response are read within that opening mercy.
findings.reader_payoff: The severe diagnosis and the communal way out belong to one mercy-framed utterance; the exception becomes legible within a named relation of care, not as a detached checklist.
findings.containment: The opening retains its plain mercy sense. The sequence supports a framing relation, not a claim that the text explicitly says mercy caused every condition or makes rescue automatic.

epistemic.reason: The two focus carriers and the diagnosis/exception sequence are supplied directly. The frame is supported by a trusted publication and attributed reader-walk evidence, while its causal reach is limited.
